options: One automatic, tenant-wide data lake underlying every Fabric workspace — not something provisioned per project
A separate lake a team must manually create for each new workspace
A Power BI feature unrelated to Lakehouses or Warehouses
A synonym for a Fabric capacity
questions.explain: OneLake exists the moment the Fabric tenant does and every workspace draws from it — nobody provisions a separate lake per project the way you might spin up a new storage account.

questions.q: According to the structure diagram in this lesson, what actually gets stored in OneLake?
options: Every Lakehouse, Warehouse, and Semantic model's data, as folders and files
Only Power BI reports, nothing else
Only data uploaded directly through OneLake File Explorer
Nothing — OneLake is just a name for the Fabric admin portal
questions.explain: Microsoft's own diagram shows a Fabric workspace containing a Lakehouse, Warehouse, and Semantic model, each holding its actual data as folders/files inside OneLake.

questions.q: Why does sharing one lake across every Fabric workload change how governance has to work?
options: Governance has to be applied at the OneLake layer itself (permissions, security roles, auditing), not separately per tool
It means governance is no longer necessary at all
It means each tool still needs its own completely separate governance system
It only affects billing, not security
questions.explain: Because every workload reads from the same underlying lake, a permission mistake isn't boxed into one product — governance has to be applied at the shared OneLake layer rather than per tool.

questions.q: What does OneLake File Explorer do?
options: Brings OneLake directly into Windows File Explorer, synced like OneDrive, using the same OneLake permissions
Creates a separate, independent set of permissions from the Fabric web UI
Lets you browse OneLake only from within a Lakehouse notebook
Replaces the need for workspace roles entirely
questions.explain: OneLake File Explorer syncs OneLake into Windows File Explorer the same way OneDrive does. It doesn't create separate permissions — it's the same OneLake and the same security, just a different window onto it.

questions.q: What does the Domain filter on the OneLake catalog do, as shown in this lesson's screenshot?
options: Scopes the catalog's item list to only the items assigned to that domain (e.g. Finance)
Deletes items not assigned to the selected domain
Changes which capacity a workspace is billed against
Grants workspace Admin access to everyone in that domain
questions.explain: Filtering the OneLake catalog by domain scopes discovery the same way access can be scoped — a user with the Finance filter applied sees Finance's items, not the whole tenant's catalog.
